formdata.value: Bioefficacy of Trichoderma  asperellum and Penicillium raperi filtrate culture consortium for suppressing bacterial stalk  rot disease (Dickeya zeae) and improving the initial growth of corn seedlings

Bioefficacy of Trichoderma  asperellum and Penicillium raperi filtrate culture consortium for suppressing bacterial stalk  rot disease (Dickeya zeae) and improving the initial growth of corn seedlings

{"judul_eng":"Bioefficacy of Trichoderma  asperellum and Penicillium raperi filtrate culture consortium for suppressing bacterial stalk  rot disease (Dickeya zeae) and improving the initial growth of corn seedlings","abstract_english":"Dickeya zeae is an emerging cosmopolitan soil-borne pathogenic bacterium that causes corn stalk rot 
disease in Indonesia. Environmentally friendly control using antagonistic fungal filtrates is an effective and efficient 
alternative option for suppressing this pathogen’s progression. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of the Tricho
derma asperellum and Penicillium raperi filtrate culture, either singly or in consortium, in suppressing the growth 
and development of D. zeae and improving the initial growth of corn seedlings. The BusbakSR22 bacterial isolate was identified as D. zeae with a genetic distance coefficient of 0.001–0.007 
and homology > 98%. There were three consortium treatments (6A-7A-9, 6A-02-10, 7A-02-10) and three single treat
ments (CHM01, HMRP9, HMRP10) which were significantly able to suppress the growth of D. zeae colonies on NA 
media with inhibition percentages ranging from 36.60 to 65.58%. The 6A-7A-9 and 7A-02-10 consortium treat
ments were consistently able to suppress the bacterial stalk rot disease progression inside a screen house and act 
as a biostimulant in improving corn seedling growth, especially maximum growth potential, growth rate, and vigor 
index. The 7A-02-10 consortium treatment consistently showed better performance than the other treatments 
in suppressing the growth and development of D. zeae both in vitro and in planta and improving the growth of corn 
seedlings.","abstrak_indonesia":"Dickeya zeae adalah bakteri patogen yang muncul dan bersifat kosmopolitan yang menyebabkan penyakit busuk batang jagung di Indonesia. Pengendalian yang ramah lingkungan menggunakan filtrat jamur antagonis adalah opsi alternatif yang efektif dan efisien untuk menekan perkembangan patogen ini. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi efikasi kultur filtrat Trichoderma asperellum dan Penicillium raperi, baik secara tunggal maupun dalam konsorsium, dalam menekan pertumbuhan dan perkembangan D. zeae serta meningkatkan pertumbuhan awal bibit jagung. Isolat bakteri BusbakSR22 diidentifikasi sebagai D. zeae dengan koefisien jarak genetik 0,001–0,007 dan homologi > 98%. Terdapat tiga perlakuan konsorsium (6A-7A-9, 6A-02-10, 7A-02-10) dan tiga perlakuan tunggal (CHM01, HMRP9, HMRP10) yang secara signifikan mampu menekan pertumbuhan koloni D. zeae pada media NA dengan persentase penghambatan berkisar antara 36,60 hingga 65,58%. Perlakuan konsorsium 6A-7A-9 dan 7A-02-10 secara konsisten mampu menekan perkembangan penyakit busuk batang bakteri di dalam rumah layar dan bertindak sebagai biostimulan dalam meningkatkan pertumbuhan benih jagung, terutama potensi pertumbuhan maksimum, laju pertumbuhan, dan indeks vigor. Perlakuan konsorsium 7A-02-10 secara konsisten menunjukkan kinerja yang lebih baik dibandingkan perlakuan lainnya dalam menekan pertumbuhan dan perkembangan D. zeae baik in vitro maupun in planta serta meningkatkan pertumbuhan benih jagung.","nama_jurnal":"EGYPTIAN JOURNAL OF BIOLOGICAL PEST CONTROL","issn":"11101768","e_issn":"25369342","tahun":2025,"reputasi":"Jurnal Ilmiah Terindeks Global Bereputasi Tinggi","penerbit":"Springer Nature","doi":"https://doi.org/10.1186/s41938-024-00827-y","halaman":"15","subindeksasi":"Q1","ref_subindeksasi_id":4,"ref_bahasa_id":5,"url_publikasi":"","biaya_layanan_elsa":[],"catatan":"","tanggal_accepted":"2024-10-24","status_publikasi":"accepted"}
